assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and credit cycles gave the modern account of how small shocks are amplified and persist through balance sheets. The framework underlies macro-financial modelling, policy analysis after 2008, and much applied work on financial frictions. The impact is broad and has lasted decades.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) is the core contribution. Gertler's work, with Bernanke and Gilchrist on the financial accelerator, is closely linked and widens the framework's reach. Bernanke is not on this ballot and already shared the 2022 prize for banking and crises. Whether to credit Gertler or Gilchrist is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from the 1990s and have been tested and extended for about three decades. The claim is mature, and the prize committee has plenty of evidence to work with.
uncertainties: The 2022 prize on banks and financial crises may lessen the perceived novelty of the macro-finance area.
Choosing between the Kiyotaki-Moore and Bernanke-Gertler lines, and who among Gertler and Gilchrist to include.
Empirical identification of collateral channels is less clean than the theory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The law and finance programme created a large empirical literature linking legal origins and investor protection to financial development, ownership structure and growth. It reshaped comparative corporate finance and institutional economics. Its influence on research and policy debate is very broad.
assessment.attribution: The 'Law and Finance' and 'Legal Determinants of External Finance' papers are by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. Vishny is credited but is left out because of the three-laureate cap. Shleifer's wider body of work is also large. Attribution among four co-authors is a real difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The papers date from 1997-2008 and have been replicated, extended and challenged for over two decades. The legal-origins hypothesis has also faced sustained criticism.
uncertainties: The legal origins thesis is contested, with critiques on measurement, endogeneity and historical interpretation.
Four-way attribution against a three-laureate cap.
Conduct controversies around one candidate may influence committee views, though they are not adjudicated here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed international trade theory and empirics after the Krugman 2008 prize. It explains why trade raises aggregate productivity through reallocation and links micro firm data to welfare. It has been highly influential and has led to extensive empirical work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central paper. Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) and Helpman's broader trade work add important contributions. Redding is a strong contributor to quantitative extensions. A two-person award is clean, while a three-person one would be defensible.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from the early 2000s and is well established. It forms the standard approach in the field.
uncertainties: Related quantitative trade work, such as Eaton-Kortum, Arkolakis-Costinot-Rodriguez-Clare, and Bernard-Jensen, overlaps on credit.
Whether the committee views this as a distinct discovery or an extension of the new trade theory prize.
Helpman also appears in the separate trade-politics candidate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural methods for demand estimation with differentiated products, and for dynamic industry models, underlie modern empirical industrial organisation, merger review and antitrust. The methods are widely used by researchers, competition authorities and firms. They combine methodological advances with substantial practical impact.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (BLP, 1995) is the central demand-estimation contribution. Pakes's work on dynamic games (Ericson-Pakes, Bajari-Benkard-Levin) extends this. Bresnahan, Reiss and others made important earlier structural contributions. The credit is spread over many people.
assessment.maturity: BLP is thirty years old and routinely used. The field is mature, with ample evidence of lasting influence.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse across a seven-name list, and any three-person selection omits major contributors.
Questions about the credibility of structural assumptions remain in the profession.
The committee has recently favoured other areas, so timing is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed how researchers think about what data can reveal without strong assumptions. It supports transparent bounds, credible inference and policy analysis under ambiguity. It is a foundational methodological contribution to empirical practice, though practical adoption is uneven.
assessment.attribution: Manski's work on bounds and identification from the late 1980s onward is the clear origin. Tamer and others, including Molinari, developed econometric inference methods for partially identified models. A solo or two-person award would be defensible.
assessment.maturity: The ideas date back more than 35 years and the inference literature has matured. Applied adoption has grown but remains less than for design-based approaches.
uncertainties: Impact on mainstream applied practice is less than the theoretical significance suggests.
Whether to credit Manski alone or add inference contributors.
Recent prizes to causal-inference methods (2021) may shape how the committee sees econometric candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework, with nominal rigidities, microfounded Phillips curves and interest-rate rules, became the main toolkit for monetary policy analysis in central banks. Its influence on policy practice and academic macroeconomics is very large.
assessment.attribution: Contributions are spread across Calvo (staggered pricing), Taylor (rules and staggered contracts), Woodford (the integrated framework), Gali, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans (estimated DSGE) and Smets and Wouters. Eight names are credited, making a clean three-person selection hard and unavoidably contestable.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1980s to the 2000s and is well tested. The 2008 crisis and the 2021-22 inflation episode raised questions about parts of the framework.
uncertainties: Attribution is very diffuse and a three-person cut is arbitrary.
Evidence on the framework's performance during recent inflation is mixed.
Overlap with the 2022 monetary and banking prize and earlier macro awards.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Linking population administrative data to measure intergenerational mobility and its local determinants has changed the study of inequality and opportunity. It combines large-scale measurement with quasi-experimental methods and has had large policy and public influence.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual and organisational leader of the programme. Hendren, Friedman and Katz are major collaborators, and credit is shared across large teams. Chetty's other work, on public economics, is also relevant.
assessment.maturity: The main results are from 2014 onward, which is relatively recent. Replication and long-run validation are still under way, and causal claims on neighbourhood effects are evolving.
uncertainties: Timing: the core evidence is about a decade old.
Whether the committee would rather recognise the data methodology or a specific finding.
Attribution among a large team, and the pairing with other Chetty-linked candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design supply a general framework for how a sender optimally shapes others' information, with applications in regulation, disclosure, platform design and communication. It extends the information-economics tradition recognised in the 1996 and 2020 prizes.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica and Gentzkow (2011) is the central paper. Bergemann and Morris's work on information design and robust predictions is closely related and conceptually broad. Selecting three of four credited names is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: The core work is about fifteen years old. Theory is mature, but empirical and policy validation is thinner.
uncertainties: Relatively young; real-world impact beyond theory is still developing.
Overlap with prior information-economics and mechanism-design awards.
Which pairing of persuasion and information-design contributors is appropriate.
